newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX ends at third high in a row.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX ends at third high in a row.

text.p: 1125 GMT - The Budapest Stock Exchange continued its bull run on Wednesday and added almost four percent to an over two percent gain on Tuesday.
* The BUX index finished at a third successive closing high of 8,483.79 points, up 315.66 points or 3.86 percent. During the session it set a trading high of 8,494.37 points.
* Volume of traded stocks and compensation coupons amounted to 2,397,470 units, with roughly half of it generated by oil company MOL.
* Twenty-five stocks finished higher, six lower and six steady. The coupons also closed lower.
The Budapest Stock Exchange surged almost four percent on Wednesday, setting a third successive closing high.
The BUX index finished at 8,483.79 points, up 315.66 points or 3.86 percent after setting an intra-day high of 8,494.37 points during the session.

"Foreigners seem to be very active in buying shares...huge amounts of money are flowing in with (investors) prepared to pay any price for the shares," said Tamas Revesz of Wintrust. "Funds are being filled up."
One analyst said today that earnings hopes were keeping prices firm.
"The optimism relating to general corporate earnings remains...the main underlying force," said Roger Monson, Chief Equity Strategist at Daiwa Europe in London.
Monson said the market was not cheap in central European terms, but was attractive compared to western European markets.

"If you were to put Hungary against valuations in the local central European market prospective, it looks very expensive, (but) if you put it into the perspective of Netherlands, France, Germany, Spain, Italy, then it looks moderately priced," he said.
However, with the BUX index more than doubling since the beginning of the year, a downward correction might come if there was any bad news, he said.

"A few items of bad news can pull this market back five or ten percent probably fairly easily on profit-taking," Monson said, citing disappointing inflation figures as a likely negative factor which could appear in September or October.

Several stocks set new highs on Wednesday, with OTP Bank finishing at 7,500 forints, up 600, and home improvement product maker Graboplast surging to above 13,000 forints before settling at 12,995, up 795.
Packaging company Cofinec gained 320 forints to close at 5,600 after it announced new steps in a group-wide restructuring programme it began in September 1996.
The day's most active issue, oil company MOL, which accounted for about half of the traded volume, finished at 5,215 forints, up 110.
